identity.title: Uncover Underlying Correspondence for Robust Multi-view Clustering

problem.claim: Robust multi-view clustering when cross-view data contain noisy correspondence.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies unreliable alignments caused by category-level and sample-level correspondence mismatches, including samples with no valid counterpart.

contributions.claim: CorreGen formulates noisy-correspondence learning as maximum-likelihood estimation over latent cross-view correspondences.
An EM procedure infers soft correspondences and updates embeddings; GMM-guided marginals down-weight noisy or unalignable samples.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present CorreGen as a generative framework for uncovering underlying correspondence in noisy multi-view clustering.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on synthetic and real-world noisy datasets show significantly improved clustering robustness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-view clustering relies on cross-view consistency to group unlabeled data.
Web-collected data can violate this prior through category-level and sample-level correspondence mismatch.
CorreGen models latent correspondences with maximum likelihood and solves the objective using EM with soft relations and adaptive down-weighting.
The authors report improved robustness on synthetic and real-world noisy datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates correspondence noise into category-level mismatch and sample-level misalignment, including absent counterparts, before mapping them to soft inference and adaptive weighting.

lessons.interpretation: A useful methodological pattern is to decompose a broad data-quality problem into distinct failure modes and align each with an explicit modeling response.
lessons.application: When presenting a robustness method, name the concrete corruption types, then state which mechanism addresses each type.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the failure modes cannot be distinguished from available data or when the method has only one undifferentiated remedy.

unknowns: No metrics, baselines, dataset sizes, or quantitative results are provided.
The abstract does not establish which component drives the reported improvement or whether the method handles correspondence noise beyond the described mismatch types.
